about: Trade intel the opposing GMs use: who is on the block, what each club is looking for, who is shedding salary, and each club's posture. status: available = shopping him or clearly available; listening = open to offers (price high = they want an overpay); untouchable = club has said he is not available. dump = the club is reported to want out of the contract or to move a problem player (the trade engine then treats the deal as a salary dump); ntc = full no-trade clause. Team 'win' overrides the window when reporting shows the baseline is wrong. Master copy lives in the public repo; the daily task refreshes it.

LAD.note: Swept by the Brewers in the NLCS with a tax payroll near $385M; bullpen and getting younger are the stated needs, plus a right-handed middle infielder. Expected to work by trade before a possible lockout.

NYY.note: Won 93 games, lost the ALDS; Cashman calls the bullpen his top priority, is open-minded about a new third-base plan, and wants a right-handed catcher and a second baseman.

SEA.note: After a 76-86 year, traded Bryce Miller, Ferrer and Evans to Kansas City for Maikel Garcia; Dipoto has about $30-35M to spend and still wants a right-handed outfield bat and a left-handed reliever.

BOS.note: All in: a big-market playoff team that has been the most aggressive AL East club this winter. Still needs a starter (four of its top five are left-handed) and more power. The outfield logjam has Duran and Yoshida on the market.

MIL.note: Defending World Series champion keeping its core; needs right-handed relief, a left-handed first baseman if Bauers leaves, and a backup catcher.

CLE.note: Lost the ALCS in six; Antonetti says payroll (lowest in MLB in 2026) will go up and a starter by trade or free agency is a primary goal.

TBR.note: Won the pennant, lost the World Series; the rotation is the big question with Peralta and Martinez free agents. Some payroll flexibility under the new owner.

MIN.note: Finished 77-85 but is buying: ownership vowed a higher payroll, Sonny Gray signed and Jeffers accepted the qualifying offer. The bullpen is the top need, then a middle-of-the-order bat.

TOR.note: Fell to 79-83 a year after the World Series; wants one or two power bats, long-term outfielders, a reshaped middle infield and back-end rotation help. No sign of cutting payroll.

DET.note: Traded Skubal and Mize at the 2026 deadline but did not rebuild; expected to compete for the division around a young core. Signed Emilio Pagan and wants more relievers.

PHI.note: Dombrowski must add an outfielder and a top setup man; third base is open. About $280M in tax commitments limits him, and the club is reported to want a shake-up.

ATL.note: Won the NL East and returns its core; starting pitching is the clear top need, then shortstop, left field and the bullpen.

PIT.note: First winning season since 2018; Cherington says the club is not financially constrained and will attack free agency and trades.

CHC.note: Lost in the Wild Card round and has 15 free agents, including all five season-ending starters; Hoyer says pitching is the focus.

HOU.note: Won the AL West, swept in the Wild Card round; new GM Randy Flores. Owner Jim Crane does not expect a teardown. Thin in the outfield and rotation, with one infielder too many now that Correa is healthy.

ATH.note: Young club with its hitters signed long term; the need is pitching: a proven starter and a closer.

BAL.note: Missed the playoffs again and traded Rutschman at the deadline; reported to be listening on everyone except Pete Alonso while it looks for a starter, an outfielder and a catcher.

TEX.note: Third straight losing season; Chris Young says payroll stays near $190M and he is very open-minded on trades, including stars. Reported to be exploring a way out of part of Corey Seager's contract.

CHW.note: A breakthrough 2026 has Getz talking about improving a contender early in its window; impact starting pitching is the top priority even after signing Dustin May.

ARI.note: Trying to win in 2027, but Hazen says payroll comes down from 2026's franchise record. The Ketel Marte decision drives the winter.

MIA.note: Bendix wants to build on a promising 2026: at least one starter and one reliever, catching help, and he is open to an everyday corner bat.

KCR.note: Went 69-93 and is aiming for a 2027 rebound around Bobby Witt Jr.; about $30M is coming off the payroll to reinvest. Wants a right-handed outfielder; third base is open after the Maikel Garcia trade.

STL.note: Still rebuilding under Chaim Bloom with a bottom-three payroll; only short-term veterans expected, rotation and bullpen first.

WSN.note: Went 77-85, the most wins since 2019; Toboni says pitching is the main need, rotation and late-inning arms.

SDP.note: Nearly the whole rotation left in free agency; Preller wants several starters and points to new owners after two budget-limited winters.

SFG.note: Finished 65-97, but Posey says the core can turn it around quickly; wants a starter, a closer and a left-handed reliever. Reported to want out of at least one of its huge contracts (Devers, Adames, Chapman).

LAA.note: Direction undecided: the club is being sold, and no GM or manager will be hired until the sale is approved. Needs a catcher, a center fielder, left-handed bats and bullpen help.

CIN.note: Finished last, but Krall says no rebuild and the aim is to contend in 2027; wants starting pitching, a No. 1 catcher and bullpen help, and is open to trading veterans.

COL.note: Won 58 games, 15 better than 2025; DePodesta's priority is starting pitching through trades and established free agents, says investment will be equal or larger and nothing is driven by money.

NYM.note: After selling at the 2026 deadline, Stearns says the rotation is the top priority, then the bullpen and a first baseman; expects Cohen's usual backing.
